display_title: [XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

`CanonicalizeDot` reshaped both operands with the lhs batch dimensions. When a batch dimension is dynamic in the lhs but static in the rhs, the canonical rhs got a dynamic dimension with no size, and `DynamicPadder` failed on the dot with "Dynamic input unexpectedly found for unsupported instruction". The lhs batch dimensions were also collected in operand order instead of `lhs_batch_dimensions` order, which moved the dynamic flag to the wrong dimension when the batch dimension numbers were not sorted.

Each operand now keeps its own batch dimensions, in dimension-number order. The shape of the canonical dot comes from `ShapeInference::InferDotOpShape` instead of being built by hand, so it takes its batch dimensions from the lhs as shape inference does.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49340. Imported from https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49346.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029896085

display_title: [XLA] Use i64 scan indices when padded mhlo.scan exceeds INT32_MAX.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use i64 scan indices when padded mhlo.scan exceeds INT32_MAX.

Shardy's `mhlo.scan` partitioning previously hardcoded `i32` for the global and local scan index tensors and truncated the unpadded scan size via `static_cast<int32_t>`. When the padded scan dimension exceeds `INT32_MAX`, the 32-bit `iota` and limit constant overflow and misidentify the last shard.

We now select `i64` for the scan index tensors and limit constant whenever the padded scan dimension requires 64-bit offsets, keeping `i32` for smaller shapes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029889537

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use llvm::StringLiteral for kNoFpContractAttr.

`kNoFpContractAttr` in `xla/service/llvm_ir/llvm_util.h` was declared as `absl::string_view` and passed directly to `llvm::Function::hasFnAttribute` and `addFnAttr`, which take `llvm::StringRef`. On toolchains such as the Android NDK where `absl::string_view` is not an alias for `std::string_view`, there is no implicit conversion to `llvm::StringRef` and compilation fails.

Declare `kNoFpContractAttr` as `llvm::StringLiteral` so that it converts directly to `llvm::StringRef` across all toolchains.

display_title: [XLA] Keep the dot algorithm when importing 2-D dots to StableHLO

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep the dot algorithm when importing 2-D dots to StableHLO

**Why**

A sharded `jax.jit` program partitioned with Shardy (the default partitioner)
that calls `jnp.dot(a, b, precision=jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset.F32_F32_F32)`
on 2-D operands silently runs at default precision. On GPU that is TF32: the
relative error is 2.9e-4 instead of 2.9e-7. `TF32_TF32_F32_X3` and
`BF16_BF16_F32_X6` show the same error. With GSPMD the results are correct.
Reported in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53163.

**Root cause**

Shardy round-trips the module through StableHLO. On import,
`HloFunctionImporter` turns a dot with default dimension numbers (vector or
matrix operands, no batch dimensions) into `stablehlo.dot`. `stablehlo.dot` has
no `algorithm` attribute, so the algorithm is only kept as a discardable
attribute, and the export to HLO drops it. Dots with batch dimensions already
import as `stablehlo.dot_general`, which keeps the algorithm.

**Fix**

`DotIsDefault` now returns false for a dot with an algorithm. Such dots take the
existing `stablehlo.dot_general` path, the same path batched algorithm dots
already use. Dots without an algorithm still import as `stablehlo.dot`. A 2-D
dot with an algorithm still exports to an HLO `dot` with the same dimension
numbers, and now keeps its algorithm.

**Testing**

Added `xla/hlo/translate/tests/dot_algorithm_import.hlo`. It checks that a 2-D
dot with `algorithm=dot_f32_f32_f32` imports as `stablehlo.dot_general` with the
algorithm, and that the algorithm is still there after HLO -> StableHLO -> HLO.
The test fails without the fix.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026602448

display_title: [XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

HloSharding stores tuple shardings as a flat pre-order list of leaf shardings.
Previously, `HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` recursively parsed
`tuple_shardings` elements without rejecting nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` entries,
allowing nested tuple `HloSharding` objects that violated the flat-leaf
invariant (causing downstream `CHECK(!sharding.IsTuple())` aborts such as in
`GetSubSharding`) and permitting unbounded recursion on deeply nested protos.

Reject nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` elements before recursing in
`HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` with `InvalidArgumentError`, add a `DCHECK`
enforcing flat leaves in the private tuple constructor, guard
`ValidateNonTuple` against nested tuple elements, flatten tuple entry-argument
shardings (expanding unannotated tuple args by leaf count) in
`SetEntryTupleShardings` (and handle tuple shapes/shardings in
`RewriteLayoutWithShardedShape`), and clarify the `named_sharding` tuple
comments in `hlo_sharding.h` and `xla_data.proto`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029877543

display_title: [xla:gpu] Use `shared_memory_per_block_optin` for `GpuTargetConfig.smem_capacity_bytes`

head_commit.message:
[xla:gpu] Use `shared_memory_per_block_optin` for `GpuTargetConfig.smem_capacity_bytes`

`smem_capacity_bytes` previously returned `shared_memory_per_core()`, which includes reserved per-block shared memory and exceeds the maximum a single block can allocate (e.g., 1 KiB higher on H100/A100, 30 KiB higher on RTX 6000 Pro). Returning `shared_memory_per_block_optin()` matches what PJRT GPU devices expose and what GPU kernels can allocate per block.

display_title: [XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

`Mesh::FromProto` and `AxisRef::FromProto` crashed with `CHECK` failures on
malformed protos (including invalid axis sizes, axis-size product overflow,
mismatched device id counts, invalid device id permutations, and invalid
sub-axes).

Both now return `absl::StatusOr`. Add `Mesh::TryCreate` (canonicalizing
empty-axes device assignments to `TileAssignment()` or
`TileAssignment(device_id)`), add an early `reshape_dims`/`transpose_perm`
size check in `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate`, validate sub-axes with
`AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis`, guard empty-span `std::memcpy`/`std::memmove`
in `Array`, and convert `Mesh::FromProto`'s size, overflow, and device-id
count checks to return `InvalidArgumentError` before allocating. Callers
that cannot yet propagate errors unwrap the result.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

`CanonicalizeDot` reshaped both operands with the lhs batch dimensions. When a batch dimension is dynamic in the lhs but static in the rhs, the canonical rhs got a dynamic dimension with no size, and `DynamicPadder` failed on the dot with "Dynamic input unexpectedly found for unsupported instruction". The lhs batch dimensions were also collected in operand order instead of `lhs_batch_dimensions` order, which moved the dynamic flag to the wrong dimension when the batch dimension numbers were not sorted.

Each operand now keeps its own batch dimensions, in dimension-number order. The shape of the canonical dot comes from `ShapeInference::InferDotOpShape` instead of being built by hand, so it takes its batch dimensions from the lhs as shape inference does.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49340. Imported from https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49346.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029799278

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Use llvm::StringLiteral for kNoFpContractAttr.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use llvm::StringLiteral for kNoFpContractAttr.

`kNoFpContractAttr` in `xla/service/llvm_ir/llvm_util.h` was declared as `absl::string_view` and passed directly to `llvm::Function::hasFnAttribute` and `addFnAttr`, which take `llvm::StringRef`. On toolchains such as the Android NDK where `absl::string_view` is not an alias for `std::string_view`, there is no implicit conversion to `llvm::StringRef` and compilation fails.

Declare `kNoFpContractAttr` as `llvm::StringLiteral` so that it converts directly to `llvm::StringRef` across all toolchains.

display_title: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR3)

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Read advanced_configuration in the ROCm GpuTracer

Third of three PRs to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. It connects #48502's parser to GpuTracer, so a
capture can set gpu_max_callback_api_events, gpu_max_annotation_strings
and gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task, as on CUDA. Until now the ROCm
tracer ignored these keys. gpu_max_activity_api_events is accepted but
not enforced yet.

--xla_gpu_rocm_max_trace_events keeps working, and a key overrides it
for its own limit. The flag's code is unchanged.

A bad gpu_* key is reported in XSpace.errors and the GPU trace is still
collected. With raise_error_on_start_failure, Start() fails with
InvalidArgument instead, before anything is enabled.

Drops over the callback limit are counted and reported once per
capture, in one log line and one XSpace warning, instead of one warning
per dropped HIP call.

New GPU test device_tracer_rocm_test, with 4 tests:
BadKeyStillProducesATraceAndReportsIt,
RaiseErrorOnStartFailureMakesABadKeyFatal, CallbackLimitKeyIsApplied and
CallbackLimitKeyOverridesFlag.

head_commit.message:
Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

Updates `.github/workflows/bazel_dependency_violations.yml` to run 3 parallel
jobs—one per build configuration:
- `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: consolidates the 3 CPU checks (`gpu`,
  `cuda-only`, `rocm-only`) into separate steps sharing one warm Bazel server,
  saving ~2 cold runner invocations per PR while preserving per-tag step
  reporting and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` output.
- `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build` (`--config=cuda_clang`)
- `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build` (`--config=rocm_clang_hermetic`)

Extracts the per-tag `bazel cquery` check into
`build_tools/dependencies/check_dependency_violations.sh`, triggers `cquery`
when the workflow or dependency-check scripts themselves change, and bumps the
job timeout to 15 minutes to accommodate the hermetic ROCm download.

head_commit.message:
Bump rules_ml_toolchain and depend on cuda_config in dso_loader and cuda_root_path

- Bumps `rules_ml_toolchain` in `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace3.bzl` to
  `c3a7158891712f5dba4a431b435f29f18df3fc67`
  (https://github.com/google-ml-infra/rules_ml_toolchain/pull/366), which adds
  `@local_config_cuda//cuda:cuda_config` and tags CUDA/NCCL/NVSHMEM and ROCm
  targets with `gpu`/`cuda-only`/`rocm-only`.
- Switches `//xla/tsl/platform/default:dso_loader` and
  `//xla/tsl/platform/default:cuda_root_path` from
  `@local_config_cuda//cuda:cuda_headers` to
  `@local_config_cuda//cuda:cuda_config` (and `dso_loader` from `rocm_headers`
  to `rocm_config`) since they only include `cuda_config.h` / `rocm_config.h`,
  preventing `cuda-only` targets from leaking into CPU/ROCm dependency graphs.
- Adds the missing direct `@local_config_cuda//cuda:cuda_headers` dependency to
  `//xla/tsl/cuda:cudnn_stub` (previously provided transitively via
  `dso_loader`, needed because `cudnn.h` includes `cuda_runtime_api.h`).

display_title: [XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Return errors from Mesh and AxisRef FromProto

`Mesh::FromProto` and `AxisRef::FromProto` crashed with `CHECK` failures on
malformed protos (including invalid axis sizes, axis-size product overflow,
mismatched device id counts, invalid device id permutations, and invalid
sub-axes).

Both now return `absl::StatusOr`. Add `Mesh::TryCreate` (canonicalizing
empty-axes device assignments to `TileAssignment()` or
`TileAssignment(device_id)`), add an early `reshape_dims`/`transpose_perm`
size check in `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate`, validate sub-axes with
`AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis`, guard empty-span `std::memcpy`/`std::memmove`
in `Array`, and convert `Mesh::FromProto`'s size, overflow, and device-id
count checks to return `InvalidArgumentError` before allocating. Callers
that cannot yet propagate errors unwrap the result.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_types.{h,cc}` (shared key/value type support checks used by both `SortRewriter` and `cub_sort_planner`, replacing the duplicated predicate in `sort_rewriter.cc`).
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028918425

display_title: [XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

HloSharding stores tuple shardings as a flat pre-order list of leaf shardings.
Previously, `HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` recursively parsed
`tuple_shardings` elements without rejecting nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` entries,
allowing nested tuple `HloSharding` objects that violated the flat-leaf
invariant (causing downstream `CHECK(!sharding.IsTuple())` aborts such as in
`GetSubSharding`) and permitting unbounded recursion on deeply nested protos.

Reject nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` elements before recursing in
`HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` with `InvalidArgumentError`, add a `DCHECK`
enforcing flat leaves in the private tuple constructor, guard
`ValidateNonTuple` against nested tuple elements, flatten tuple entry-argument
shardings (expanding unannotated tuple args by leaf count) in
`SetEntryTupleShardings` (and handle tuple shapes/shardings in
`RewriteLayoutWithShardedShape`), and clarify the `named_sharding` tuple
comments in `hlo_sharding.h` and `xla_data.proto`.

display_title: [XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep each operand's own batch dimensions in DotDecomposer

`CanonicalizeDot` reshaped both operands with the lhs batch dimensions. When a batch dimension is dynamic in the lhs but static in the rhs, the canonical rhs got a dynamic dimension with no size, and `DynamicPadder` failed on the dot with "Dynamic input unexpectedly found for unsupported instruction". The lhs batch dimensions were also collected in operand order instead of `lhs_batch_dimensions` order, which moved the dynamic flag to the wrong dimension when the batch dimension numbers were not sorted.

Each operand now keeps its own batch dimensions, in dimension-number order. The shape of the canonical dot comes from `ShapeInference::InferDotOpShape` instead of being built by hand, so it takes its batch dimensions from the lhs as shape inference does.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49340. Imported from https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49346.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

`SortRewriter` runs before `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, and its heuristics (as well as `Mode::kAlways`) currently rewrite some zero-element shapes (such as `f16[0, 4096]` on Blackwell or `u8[0, 2000]` on A100/H100) and single-element segment shapes (such as `u8[1]` on A100/H100 or `f32[20000, 1]` on the fallback heuristic) into `cub_sort` custom calls. Once rewritten into a tuple-output custom call, neither `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleSort` nor `ZeroSizedHloElimination` eliminates them.

So this change rejects `total_items == 0 || segment_size <= 1` in `IsCubCompatibleSort` in `xla/backends/gpu/hlo/transforms/sort_rewriter.cc`. Those degenerate `sort` ops then remain regular `kSort` instructions and are folded away by `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` (or handled as no-ops / copies by the fallback sort emitter if simplification is disabled), and downstream CUB sort code no longer needs to handle degenerate sizes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029835389

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_types.{h,cc}` (shared key/value type support checks used by both `SortRewriter` and `cub_sort_planner`, replacing the duplicated predicate in `sort_rewriter.cc`).
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

head_commit.message:
Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

A PJRT client can attach user data and a destructor to a `PJRT_Memory` through
`set_user_data`. The C API client in `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client.cc`
does this for every addressable memory. The plugin then calls that client
destructor when it replaces the data and in `PJRT_Client_Destroy`.

The client is sometimes a separately built library, such as a Python wheel. If
the plugin uses `-fsanitize=kcfi` in that case, the client destructor has no
matching kCFI type hash. The call then traps with SIGILL.

This change skips the kCFI check only for the destructor calls. The rest of the
file keeps its kCFI checks, including the `get_user_data` calls.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029832899

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.6-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. If it has a .jsonl file, use gh to verify the package:

$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)

display_title: PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

head_commit.message:
PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53038

#ai-generated

**Status quo**
`WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory` and `WindowsFileSystem::DeleteRecursively` convert the wide-character path back to `std::string` by range-constructing it from the `std::wstring`, which keeps only the low byte of each wide character. Any path segment above U+007F — a user folder like 王小明 or café — is mangled, so `IsDirectory` fails on directories that exist and `DeleteRecursively` works on a wrong name. In TensorFlow this breaks the flows built on these calls (`isdir`, `makedirs`, `saved_model.save`, `CheckpointManager.save`) for non-ASCII directory names on Windows. Real users hit this in tensorflow/tensorflow#62691 and tensorflow/tensorflow#61550; both were closed as stale without a fix.

**Why**
Non-ASCII user and folder names are the default outside English locales, and saving a model or a checkpoint into such a folder is a basic flow, not an edge case. The reports were closed for staleness, not because the bug went away.

**Design**
Convert with the existing `WideCharToUtf8()` helper instead of the truncating range constructor, in both places (two lines). No other call sites change.

**Testing**
New `EnvTest.NonAsciiDirectoryNames` in `xla/tsl/platform/env_test.cc`: creates `café/王`, checks `RecursivelyCreateDir`, `IsDirectory` on both levels, writes a file, then `DeleteRecursively` and confirms the tree is gone. Reproduced with TensorFlow 2.21.0: the two changed functions return NotFound before and OK after.

One honest limitation: XLA's GitHub CI has no Windows job, so this test's Windows coverage only runs downstream (e.g. TensorFlow's Windows builds). On Linux the test passes either way, since UTF-8 paths are native there.

[XLA/TSL] Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory for non-ASCII paths

IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively turned the wide UNC path back into a
std::string by narrowing each wchar_t to a char. For any non-ASCII
character that drops the high byte (U+00E9 becomes 0xE9, U+738B becomes
0x8B), so the FileExists() call that follows looks up a different, invalid
UTF-8 name and fails. Convert with WideCharToUtf8() instead, as the rest of
the file does.

On Windows this made IsDirectory fail for every directory whose path
contains a non-ASCII character, which breaks RecursivelyCreateDir under
such a directory, GetMatchingPaths patterns that recurse into it, Stat's
is_directory, and DeleteRecursively.

Merging this change closes #53038

PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

#ai-generated

**Status quo**
`WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory` and `WindowsFileSystem::DeleteRecursively` convert the wide-character path back to `std::string` by range-constructing it from the `std::wstring`, which keeps only the low byte of each wide character. **Why**
Non-ASCII user and folder names are the default outside English locales, and saving a model or a checkpoint into such a folder is a basic flow, not an edge case. The reports were closed for staleness, not because the bug went away.

**Design**
Convert with the existing `WideCharToUtf8()` helper instead of the truncating range constructor, in both places (two lines). No other call sites change.

**Testing**

head_commit.message:
Return +inf from Digamma at -0.0

Digamma's limit at zero is -inf from the right and +inf from the left,
so the sign of the zero picks the side. Digamma returned -inf for both

that inline Digamma pick up the extra IsNegZero select.

Follow-up to #47754, see tensorflow/tensorflow#121498.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

`SortRewriter` runs before `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, and its heuristics (as well as `Mode::kAlways`) currently rewrite some zero-element shapes (such as `f16[0, 4096]` on Blackwell or `u8[0, 2000]` on A100/H100) and single-element segment shapes (such as `u8[1]` on A100/H100 or `f32[20000, 1]` on the fallback heuristic) into `cub_sort` custom calls. Once rewritten into a tuple-output custom call, neither `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleSort` nor `ZeroSizedHloElimination` eliminates them.

So this change rejects `total_items == 0 || segment_size <= 1` in `IsCubCompatibleSort` in `xla/backends/gpu/hlo/transforms/sort_rewriter.cc`. Those degenerate `sort` ops then remain regular `kSort` instructions and are folded away by `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` (or handled as no-ops / copies by the fallback sort emitter if simplification is disabled), and downstream CUB sort code no longer needs to handle degenerate sizes.

display_title: [XLA] Bound the multi output fusion cycle search by topological levels

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound the multi output fusion cycle search by topological levels

Before each multi output fusion, InstructionFusion::RunImpl checks that the
producer cannot reach another operand of the consumer by walking its whole
forward cone. Most of that cone lies past the consumer, where no operand of
the consumer can be. The loop now keeps a topological level per instruction,
computed once per computation with room between layers, and raised forward
after each fusion through the instructions between the producer and the
consumer. The walk skips instructions at or above the consumer's level.
Output is unchanged; the tests cover nested raises and fusion hooks that add
instructions.

display_title: Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

head_commit.message:
Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

A PJRT client can attach user data and a destructor to a `PJRT_Memory` through
`set_user_data`. The C API client in `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client.cc`
does this for every addressable memory. The plugin then calls that client
destructor when it replaces the data and in `PJRT_Client_Destroy`.

The client is sometimes a separately built library, such as a Python wheel. If
the plugin uses `-fsanitize=kcfi` in that case, the client destructor has no
matching kCFI type hash. The call then traps with SIGILL.

This change skips the kCFI check only for the destructor calls. The rest of the
file keeps its kCFI checks, including the `get_user_data` calls.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029697205

PR #53334: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53334

📝 Summary of Changes
TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass now also squeezes a tt.reduce over a [1, N] row tile:
it becomes a 1D reduce plus tt.splat, so the row stays in one layout.

🎯 Justification
Softmax and RMSNorm fusions with 1xN row tiles converted each row through shared
memory and computed elementwise ops twice. With 16 warps, 32K-element rows
failed to compile on MI200/MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, ⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
MI350X, default configs: up to 33% less kernel time for softmax and 15% for
RMSNorm

🧪 Unit Tests:
4 FileCheck cases in triton_xla_squeeze_dims.mlir (rewrite, expand_dims case,
splat fold, multi-row skip). triton_single_row_reduction.hlo compiles a 1x32768
RMSNorm fusion with 16 warps; it fails on mi200/mi300 without the fix.

[XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass kept the unit dimension of a tt.reduce over a [1, N]
row tile, as the result Triton converted the whole row between layouts through
shared memory. Rewrite such reduces as a 1D reduce plus tt.splat.
This cuts MI350X kernel time by up to 33% (softmax) and 15% (RMSNorm), and
lets 1x32768 tiles with 16 warps compile on MI200/MI300 - avoid error:
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Shared memory size limit exceeded.

display_title: PR #53334: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

head_commit.message:
PR #53334: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53334

📝 Summary of Changes
TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass now also squeezes a tt.reduce over a [1, N] row tile:
it becomes a 1D reduce plus tt.splat, so the row stays in one layout.

🎯 Justification
Softmax and RMSNorm fusions with 1xN row tiles converted each row through shared
memory and computed elementwise ops twice. With 16 warps, 32K-element rows
failed to compile on MI200/MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, ⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
MI350X, default configs: up to 33% less kernel time for softmax and 15% for
RMSNorm

🧪 Unit Tests:
4 FileCheck cases in triton_xla_squeeze_dims.mlir (rewrite, expand_dims case,
splat fold, multi-row skip). triton_single_row_reduction.hlo compiles a 1x32768
RMSNorm fusion with 16 warps; it fails on mi200/mi300 without the fix.

Copybara import of the project:

--
7a64e06637506b27e89262ca29a858814af82b52 by Zoran Jovanovic <zjovanov@amd.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass kept the unit dimension of a tt.reduce over a [1, N]
row tile, as the result Triton converted the whole row between layouts through
shared memory. Rewrite such reduces as a 1D reduce plus tt.splat.
This cuts MI350X kernel time by up to 33% (softmax) and 15% (RMSNorm), and
lets 1x32768 tiles with 16 warps compile on MI200/MI300 - avoid error:
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Shared memory size limit exceeded.

Merging this change closes #53334

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow reverse scans in Triton.

The Triton scan emitter already handles reverse scans: it visits the tiles in reverse order and takes the carry from the first element of each tile. Padding a partial tile with zeros stays correct because only additive combiners are supported.

Remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`, so that `ScanRewriterTriton` also rewrites reverse scans.

display_title: [XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject nested TUPLE OpSharding protos in HloSharding::FromProto

HloSharding stores tuple shardings as a flat pre-order list of leaf shardings.
Previously, `HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` recursively parsed
`tuple_shardings` elements without rejecting nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` entries,
allowing nested tuple `HloSharding` objects that violated the flat-leaf
invariant (causing downstream `CHECK(!sharding.IsTuple())` aborts such as in
`GetSubSharding`) and permitting unbounded recursion on deeply nested protos.

Reject nested `OpSharding::TUPLE` elements before recursing in
`HloSharding::FromProtoInternal` with `InvalidArgumentError`, add a `DCHECK`
enforcing flat leaves in the private tuple constructor, guard
`ValidateNonTuple` against nested tuple elements, flatten tuple entry-argument
shardings (expanding unannotated tuple args by leaf count) in
`SetEntryTupleShardings` (and handle tuple shapes/shardings in
`RewriteLayoutWithShardedShape`), and clarify the `named_sharding` tuple
comments in `hlo_sharding.h` and `xla_data.proto`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026362286

display_title: [XLA] Bound the multi output fusion cycle search by topological levels

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound the multi output fusion cycle search by topological levels

Before each multi output fusion, InstructionFusion::RunImpl checks that the
producer cannot reach another operand of the consumer by walking its whole
forward cone. Most of that cone lies past the consumer, where no operand of
the consumer can be. The loop now keeps a topological level per instruction,
computed once per computation with room between layers, and raised forward
after each fusion through the instructions between the producer and the
consumer. The walk skips instructions at or above the consumer's level.
Output is unchanged; the tests cover nested raises and fusion hooks that add
instructions.

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] xla_compile: instrument AOT CPU code with msan under --config=msan

Add --sanitize_memory and --sanitize_memory_track_origins to xla_compile, and
pass them from xla_aot_compile_cpu when the target is built with
--config=msan or --config=msan-track-origins. xla_compile itself runs in the
exec configuration, so its own build can't tell whether the code it generates
should be instrumented.

JIT path: the instrumented code references __msan_* runtime symbols that an
uninstrumented compiler can't resolve.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

display_title: [XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

`MeshProto::IotaTransform::transpose_perm` stores `int64` entries, but
`IotaTileAssignment::Create(dims, transform)` copied them directly into `int`
before validation. Out-of-range 64-bit values whose low 32 bits formed a valid
permutation (for example `[4294967297, 4294967296]`) were silently truncated
and accepted instead of rejected.

Add `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate(dims, const MeshProto::IotaTransform&)` to
range-check each 64-bit `transpose_perm` entry against `[0, perm_size)` before
narrowing to `int`, and delegate `Create(dims, transform)` to `TryCreate`.

display_title: [XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

A few-byte iota `OpSharding` can describe billions of devices. When its
replicated or subgroup dimensions do not align with the iota reshape
dimensions, `TryPartialTile` and `TrySubgroup` fall back to materializing an
explicit `Array<int64_t>`, so a tiny proto could allocate tens of GiB inside
`HloSharding::FromProto`.

`FromProto` now charges these iota-to-array fallbacks against a budget of 2^16
elements shared across all tuple elements, and returns InvalidArgument once it
is exceeded. Small non-aligned iota shardings still deserialize as before, and
the public `TryPartialTile`/`TrySubgroup` factories stay unlimited. `TrySubgroup`
now propagates `TryPartialTile` errors instead of CHECK-failing, and its
explicit-array fallback uses a single transpose instead of per-element index
vectors.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029766936

display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

display_title: Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

head_commit.message:
Skip kCFI checks on calls to client-supplied PJRT_Memory user data destructors.

A PJRT client can attach user data and a destructor to a `PJRT_Memory` through
`set_user_data`. The C API client in `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client.cc`
does this for every addressable memory. The plugin then calls that client
destructor when it replaces the data and in `PJRT_Client_Destroy`.

The client is sometimes a separately built library, such as a Python wheel. If
the plugin uses `-fsanitize=kcfi` in that case, the client destructor has no
matching kCFI type hash. The call then traps with SIGILL.

This change skips the kCFI check only for the destructor calls. The rest of the
file keeps its kCFI checks, including the `get_user_data` calls.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029697205

display_title: PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

head_commit.message:
PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49692

Previously, when a task failed during GPU clique initialization, `AbortCliques` only checked `state.cliques`. However, the clique isn't added there until initialization finishes, so the cancellation token was still in `pending_cliques`. I changed this so that `AbortCliques` also cancels the tokens in `pending_cliques`.

I tested this before and after the change. Before the fix, the cancellation token wasn't cancelled during initialization. After the fix, it was cancelled, allowing non-blocking initialization to stop.

This PR doesn't make blocking initialization or blocking `ncclCommSplit` check the cancellation token. For non-blocking init, the communicator handle is available before initialization finishes, so `ncclCommAbort` can clean it up if polling fails. However, for non-blocking split, `newcomm` remains `NCCL_COMM_NULL` until the split finishes, so the same cleanup doesn't work.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

display_title: [XLA] Propagate OpMetadata when simplifying dots in AlgebraicSimplifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Propagate OpMetadata when simplifying dots in AlgebraicSimplifier

Propagate the dot instruction's OpMetadata (without leaking frontend_attributes
or sharding) onto rewritten helper instructions in two AlgebraicSimplifier dot
rewrites:

- `RemoveDegenerateDimensionFromDot`: attach `dot->metadata()` to the LHS and
  RHS squeeze reshapes instead of leaving them unattributed.
- `RewriteBatchPlusContractingAsReduce`: attach `dot->metadata()` to newly
  created transposes (guarded so unmodified inputs keep their metadata),
  converts, multiply, zero constant, and reduce instructions via `AsType` and
  `AddReduce`.

Adds unit tests in `xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`
verifying metadata propagation and that input parameter metadata and dot
frontend_attributes are preserved cleanly.

display_title: [XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

`MeshProto::IotaTransform::transpose_perm` stores `int64` entries, but
`IotaTileAssignment::Create(dims, transform)` copied them directly into `int`
before validation. Out-of-range 64-bit values whose low 32 bits formed a valid
permutation (for example `[4294967297, 4294967296]`) were silently truncated
and accepted instead of rejected.

Add `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate(dims, const MeshProto::IotaTransform&)` to
range-check each 64-bit `transpose_perm` entry against `[0, perm_size)` before
narrowing to `int`, and delegate `Create(dims, transform)` to `TryCreate`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

A few-byte iota `OpSharding` can describe billions of devices. When its
replicated or subgroup dimensions do not align with the iota reshape
dimensions, `TryPartialTile` and `TrySubgroup` fall back to materializing an
explicit `Array<int64_t>`, so a tiny proto could allocate tens of GiB inside
`HloSharding::FromProto`.

`FromProto` now charges these iota-to-array fallbacks against a budget of 2^16
elements shared across all tuple elements, and returns InvalidArgument once it
is exceeded. Small non-aligned iota shardings still deserialize as before, and
the public `TryPartialTile`/`TrySubgroup` factories stay unlimited. `TrySubgroup`
now propagates `TryPartialTile` errors instead of CHECK-failing, and its
explicit-array fallback uses a single transpose instead of per-element index
vectors.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026362957

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

When multiple threads hit `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` concurrently on the same device
during execution preparation, each thread independently triggers OOM recovery
(such as program eviction and memory defragmentation) and retries at the same
time. This causes redundant double-OOM recoveries and memory thrashing.

* Add per-addressable-device `DeviceOomState` and `OomSequencer` in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.h` and `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc`.
* Add `CommonPjRtClient::RunWithOomRetries`, which runs lock-free when the
  device is not under OOM, serializes recovery and retry attempts per device on
  `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and skips redundant recovery when another thread has
  already bumped the device OOM generation.
* Route `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::ExecutePrepareWithOomRetries` through
  `RunWithOomRetries`, resetting `launch_args` before waiting or recovering so
  partial buffer holds are released first.
* Add unit tests for `OomSequencer` concurrency, serialization, generation
  skipping, termination, and per-device independence in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client_test.cc`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014145217

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

head_commit.message:
Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

`PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer::CopyRawHostToDeviceAndReturnEvent` and
`CopyRawDeviceToHostAndReturnEvent` previously did not check whether the buffer
resides on CPU (`pinned_host`), unlike `ToStagingBuffer` and
`AllocateLinearizeDest`. Raw transfers on `pinned_host` buffers therefore
allocated a second pinned staging buffer, executed `std::memcpy` inside
`stream->DoHostCallback` (stalling `cuLaunchHostFunc_v2`), and contended on
`LocalDeviceState::mu_`.

Bypass GPU transfer streams and staging buffers for CPU-accessible buffers by
dispatching `std::memcpy` on `async_work_runner()` (after `device_buffer_` is
available and any pending allocation definition event from `GetDefinitionEvent`
completes) and recording completion on a borrowed pool stream.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029679954

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

head_commit.message:
Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

`PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer::CopyRawHostToDeviceAndReturnEvent` and
`CopyRawDeviceToHostAndReturnEvent` previously did not check whether the buffer
resides on CPU (`pinned_host`), unlike `ToStagingBuffer` and
`AllocateLinearizeDest`. Raw transfers on `pinned_host` buffers therefore
allocated a second pinned staging buffer, executed `std::memcpy` inside
`stream->DoHostCallback` (stalling `cuLaunchHostFunc_v2`), and contended on
`LocalDeviceState::mu_`.

Bypass GPU transfer streams and staging buffers for CPU-accessible buffers by
dispatching `std::memcpy` on `async_work_runner()` (after `device_buffer_` is
available and any pending allocation definition event from `GetDefinitionEvent`
completes) and recording completion on a borrowed pool stream.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Create reduce-scatter through elementwise ops between all-reduce and dynamic-slice

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Match elementwise ops in MatchReduceScatter instead of moving the dynamic-slice first

ReduceScatterCreator moved the dynamic-slice next to the all-reduce before
matching, which changed the module even when no reduce-scatter was created
afterwards.

Add allow_intervening_elementwise to MatchReduceScatter, MatchWithDynamicSlice
and FindUniqueDynamicSliceUserFromCollective, next to the existing options for
an intervening reshape or bitcast. With it, the dynamic-slice is also found
through a chain of single-user copies and elementwise operations whose other
operands are scalar broadcasts, and the chain is returned in
ReduceScatterSpec::intervening_elementwise. The option is off by default, so
other users of the matcher are not affected.

ReduceScatterCreator now only modifies the module after a successful match: it
creates the reduce-scatter and re-creates the intermediate operations on its
result.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

`SortRewriter` runs before `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, and its heuristics (as well as `Mode::kAlways`) currently rewrite some zero-element shapes (such as `f16[0, 4096]` on Blackwell or `u8[0, 2000]` on A100/H100) and single-element segment shapes (such as `u8[1]` on A100/H100 or `f32[20000, 1]` on the fallback heuristic) into `cub_sort` custom calls. Once rewritten into a tuple-output custom call, neither `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleSort` nor `ZeroSizedHloElimination` eliminates them.

So this change rejects `total_items == 0 || segment_size <= 1` in `IsCubCompatibleSort` in `xla/backends/gpu/hlo/transforms/sort_rewriter.cc`. Those degenerate `sort` ops then remain regular `kSort` instructions and are folded away by `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` (or handled as no-ops / copies by the fallback sort emitter if simplification is disabled), and downstream CUB sort code no longer needs to handle degenerate sizes.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

Triton scans had two requirements on the scan dimension: `CanTritonHandleScan` required it to be the last logical dimension, and `ScanRewriterTriton` requires it to be physically last, i.e. minor-most in the layout. Remove the logical requirement. The physical one stays, because Triton scans over other dimensions are generally less efficient.

The logical requirement worked around a wrong launch grid. A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is logically last.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles. They are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

display_title: Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

head_commit.message:
Avoid staging and CUDA host callbacks for raw transfers on pinned_host buffers.

PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer::CopyRawHostToDeviceAndReturnEvent and
CopyRawDeviceToHostAndReturnEvent previously did not check whether the buffer
resides on CPU (pinned_host), unlike ToStagingBuffer and AllocateLinearizeDest.
Raw transfers on pinned_host buffers therefore allocated a second pinned staging
buffer, executed std::memcpy inside stream->DoHostCallback (stalling
cuLaunchHostFunc_v2), and contended on LocalDeviceState::mu_.

Bypass GPU streams and staging buffers for CPU-accessible buffers by performing
std::memcpy directly on the host and completing a BufferSequencingEvent without
a device event handle.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip empty and single-element sorts in SortRewriter

`SortRewriter` runs before `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, and its heuristics (as well as `Mode::kAlways`) currently rewrite some zero-element shapes (such as `f16[0, 4096]` on Blackwell or `u8[0, 2000]` on A100/H100) and single-element segment shapes (such as `u8[1]` on A100/H100 or `f32[20000, 1]` on the fallback heuristic) into `cub_sort` custom calls. Once rewritten into a tuple-output custom call, neither `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleSort` nor `ZeroSizedHloElimination` eliminates them.

So this change rejects `total_items == 0 || segment_size <= 1` in `IsCubCompatibleSort` in `xla/backends/gpu/hlo/transforms/sort_rewriter.cc`. Those degenerate `sort` ops then remain regular `kSort` instructions and are folded away by `ZeroSizedHloElimination` and `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` (or handled as no-ops / copies by the fallback sort emitter if simplification is disabled), and downstream CUB sort code no longer needs to handle degenerate sizes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029674415

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

Triton scans had two requirements on the scan dimension: `CanTritonHandleScan` required it to be the last logical dimension, and `ScanRewriterTriton` requires it to be physically last, i.e. minor-most in the layout. Remove the logical requirement. The physical one stays, because Triton scans over other dimensions are generally less efficient.

The logical requirement worked around a wrong launch grid. A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is logically last.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles. They are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

head_commit.message:
PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49692

Previously, when a task failed during GPU clique initialization, `AbortCliques` only checked `state.cliques`. However, the clique isn't added there until initialization finishes, so the cancellation token was still in `pending_cliques`. I changed this so that `AbortCliques` also cancels the tokens in `pending_cliques`.

I tested this before and after the change. Before the fix, the cancellation token wasn't cancelled during initialization. After the fix, it was cancelled, allowing non-blocking initialization to stop.

This PR doesn't make blocking initialization or blocking `ncclCommSplit` check the cancellation token. For non-blocking init, the communicator handle is available before initialization finishes, so `ncclCommAbort` can clean it up if polling fails. However, for non-blocking split, `newcomm` remains `NCCL_COMM_NULL` until the split finishes, so the same cleanup doesn't work.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

head_commit.message:
PR #46001: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 7th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001   <---- This PR
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions:
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting, Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported() ragged dispatch in the autotuner.
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

display_title: [XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

`GetShardedShape` in `xla/pjrt/utils.cc` previously called
`HloSharding::GetSubSharding(shape, index)` for each leaf inside
`ShapeUtil::ForEachMutableSubshape`, re-summing `ShapeUtil::GetLeafCount` across
all preceding tuple siblings on every leaf (`O(N^2)` for an N-element tuple).
Advance a flat leaf index directly across `hlo_sharding.tuple_elements()` in
pre-order DFS (`O(N)`), and handle non-tuple non-tiled shardings (such as
`REPLICATED`) on tuple shapes without crashing in `GetSubSharding`.

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

head_commit.message:
PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49692

Previously, when a task failed during GPU clique initialization, `AbortCliques` only checked `state.cliques`. However, the clique isn't added there until initialization finishes, so the cancellation token was still in `pending_cliques`. I changed this so that `AbortCliques` also cancels the tokens in `pending_cliques`.

I tested this before and after the change. Before the fix, the cancellation token wasn't cancelled during initialization. After the fix, it was cancelled, allowing non-blocking initialization to stop.

This PR doesn't make blocking initialization or blocking `ncclCommSplit` check the cancellation token. For non-blocking init, the communicator handle is available before initialization finishes, so `ncclCommAbort` can clean it up if polling fails. However, for non-blocking split, `newcomm` remains `NCCL_COMM_NULL` until the split finishes, so the same cleanup doesn't work.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025395036
