display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

This PR is the 7th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995

PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997

This PR adds autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions:
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting, Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported() ragged dispatch in the autotuner.
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

display_title: PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: [XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

`GetShardedShape` in `xla/pjrt/utils.cc` previously called
`HloSharding::GetSubSharding(shape, index)` for each leaf inside
`ShapeUtil::ForEachMutableSubshape`, re-summing `ShapeUtil::GetLeafCount` across
all preceding tuple siblings on every leaf (`O(N^2)` for an N-element tuple).
Advance a flat leaf index directly across `hlo_sharding.tuple_elements()` in
pre-order DFS (`O(N)`), and handle non-tuple non-tiled shardings (such as
`REPLICATED`) on tuple shapes without crashing in `GetSubSharding`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `OverflowSafeRoundUpTo` in `xla/overflow_util.h` and unit tests in `xla/overflow_util_test.cc`.
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

head_commit.message:
Remove absl::StatusOr from xla::ifrt::Array::pjrt_layout().

No `xla::ifrt::Array` implementation returns errors from `pjrt_layout()` except `BasicStringArray`, which returned `absl::UnimplementedError`. Returning `nullptr` from `BasicStringArray::pjrt_layout()` instead lets `Array::pjrt_layout()` return `absl_nullable std::shared_ptr<const xla::PjRtLayout>` directly and removes unnecessary error-handling boilerplate from callers.

head_commit.message:
Remove absl::StatusOr from xla::ifrt::Array::pjrt_layout().

No `xla::ifrt::Array` implementation returns errors from `pjrt_layout()` except `BasicStringArray`, which returned `absl::UnimplementedError`. Returning `nullptr` from `BasicStringArray::pjrt_layout()` instead lets `Array::pjrt_layout()` return `absl_nullable std::shared_ptr<const xla::PjRtLayout>` directly and removes unnecessary error-handling boilerplate from callers.

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

head_commit.message:
PR #53261: Implement more forwarding rules for `LayoutAssignment`

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53261

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment`'s `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` is responsible for forwarding layouts from operands to outputs as required by the input instruction's opcode. It currently only implements forwarding for async-start.

This PR refactors `SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` to use a new helper `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc`. This helper currently implements forwarding rules for async-start, async-done, tuple, gte, and opt-barrier instructions.

Follow up PRs will implement forwarding rules for the remaining opcodes.

🎯 Justification

`SetForwardedOperandResultLayouts` ensures that if a layout-changing copy had been inserted prior to an instruction that forwards inputs to outputs, the outputs reflect the new layout. This was only implemented for async-start, but we need to implement all ops that forward layouts.

`hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc` is a natural place to put these forwarding rules because they are not specific to layout assignment but are general rules that should be respected when running dataflow analyses. So, the forwarding rules have now been exposed in a new `GetForwardedInputOutputPairs` helper. This is not yet integrated into the analysis' implementation, but each of the handlers inside `UpdateInstructionValueSet` implement these forwarding rules.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test.cc`:
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasic`: Tests forwarding for tuple, gte, opt-barrier instructions.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsBasicAsyncStartDone`: Tests forwarding for basic async-start / async-done pairs.
- `GetForwardedInputOutputPairsLateBoundAsyncOutputs`: Tests forwarding for async-start / async-done when async-done late-binds outputs.

Added to `layout_assignment_test.cc`:
- `SetsForwardedLayoutsAfterCopies`: Tests that if layout assignment inserts a layout changing copy before a chain of instructions which require layout forwarding, all instructions in that chain are updated to reflect the new layout.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

`KernelThunk`, `ExecuteKernelOnStream`, `KernelThunkToString`, and
`FfiLaunchParams` still handled `se::ClusterDim` separately from
`LaunchDimensions`, while `CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()` dropped
`custom_kernel_.cluster_dims()`.

Read CTA cluster dimensions directly from `LaunchDimensions::cluster_dims()`
across GPU runtime thunks and stream launch helpers, and preserve them in
`CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()`.

To preserve 2-week forward compatibility, `KernelThunk::ToProto()` dual-writes
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` alongside `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims`.
For 6-month backward compatibility, `KernelThunk::FromProto()` falls back to
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` when `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims` is
unset.

display_title: Split LowerTensorsPass into dedicated CPU and GPU passes

head_commit.message:
Split LowerTensorsPass into dedicated CPU and GPU passes

Replace the unified `LowerTensorsPass` (`xla-lower-tensors`) in
`//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes` with separate backend passes so
XLA:CPU no longer pulls in GPU lowering patterns or `ROCDLDialect`:

- Add `xla::cpu::LowerTensorsPass` (`xla-cpu-lower-tensors`) in
  `xla/backends/cpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/lower_tensors.cc` and move the
  CPU `LowerTensorsConfig` out of `lower_tensors_common`.
- Fold `lower_tensors_patterns` into `xla::gpu::LowerTensorsPass`
  (`xla-gpu-lower-tensors`) in
  `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/lower_tensors.cc` and drop the
  `target_type` option and `DeviceSpec` dependency.
- Delete the unified `LowerTensorsPass` from
  `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes` (removing
  `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns` and
  `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect` from XLA:CPU).
- Migrate CPU and GPU callers (`fusion_compiler.cc`, `mlir_kernel_emitter.cc`,
  `nested_kernel_utils.cc`) and move backend-only lit tests (including the
  GPU-only test cases from `lower_tensors.mlir`) into their respective backend
  `transforms/tests/` directories.

display_title: PR #53101: [ROCm] Non-temporal cache hints for gfx942

head_commit.message:
PR #53101: [ROCm] Non-temporal cache hints for gfx942

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53101

📝 Summary of Changes
On MI300, MLIR kernels mark large streamed loads and stores non-temporal. Loads need a buffer of at least 16×L2 (64 MiB) that is read once; stores need one qualifying output in a contiguous kernel.

🎯 Justification
Data touched once otherwise evicts reused data from L2 and from MI300X's Infinity Cache. This helps memory-bound fusions over large buffers.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: ⚡️ Performance Improvement, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Synthetic streaming kernels of 64–512 MiB average −11.5%.

🧪 Unit Tests:
nontemporal_hints_test.cc,  lower_tensors_amdgpu_nontemporal.mlir, mlir_kernel_emitter_test.cc

display_title: [XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

`GetShardedShape` in `xla/pjrt/utils.cc` previously called
`HloSharding::GetSubSharding(shape, index)` for each leaf inside
`ShapeUtil::ForEachMutableSubshape`, re-summing `ShapeUtil::GetLeafCount` across
all preceding tuple siblings on every leaf (`O(N^2)` for an N-element tuple).
Advance a flat leaf index directly across `hlo_sharding.tuple_elements()` in
pre-order DFS (`O(N)`), and handle non-tuple non-tiled shardings (such as
`REPLICATED`) on tuple shapes without crashing in `GetSubSharding`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029442542

display_title: Align `BasicBundle` and `PjRtClient::Bundle` lifecycle, donation, and slice-size semantics with the IFRT `Bundle` contract.

head_commit.message:
Align `BasicBundle` and `PjRtClient::Bundle` lifecycle, donation, and slice-size semantics with the IFRT `Bundle` contract.

- Reject empty `Bundle` creation, empty `ConcatBundles`, and zero-sized bundle or output slices (`<= 0`) with `InvalidArgumentError`.
- Mark input arrays and bundles deleted on `kDonateInput` in `PjRtClient::Bundle`, `BasicBundle::ConcatBundles`, `BasicBundle::GetValues`, and `BasicBundle::Slice`, and skip value deletion in `BasicBundle::~BasicBundle()` when the bundle was already deleted or donated so transferred buffers remain live.
- Reject `BasicBundle::GetReadyFuture()` on deleted or donated bundles instead of returning a cached ready future.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023123581

display_title: [XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

`GetShardedShape` in `xla/pjrt/utils.cc` previously called
`HloSharding::GetSubSharding(shape, index)` for each leaf inside
`ShapeUtil::ForEachMutableSubshape`, re-summing `ShapeUtil::GetLeafCount` across
all preceding tuple siblings on every leaf (`O(N^2)` for an N-element tuple).
Advance a flat leaf index directly across `hlo_sharding.tuple_elements()` in
pre-order DFS (`O(N)`), and handle non-tuple non-tiled shardings (such as
`REPLICATED`) on tuple shapes without crashing in `GetSubSharding`.

Align `BasicBundle` and `PjRtClient::Bundle` lifecycle, donation, and slice-size semantics with the IFRT `Bundle` contract.

- Reject empty `Bundle` creation, empty `ConcatBundles`, and zero-sized bundle or output slices (`<= 0`) with `InvalidArgumentError`.
- Mark input arrays and bundles deleted on `kDonateInput` in `PjRtClient::Bundle`, `BasicBundle::ConcatBundles`, `BasicBundle::GetValues`, and `BasicBundle::Slice`, and skip value deletion in `BasicBundle::~BasicBundle()` when the bundle was already deleted or donated so transferred buffers remain live.
- Reject `BasicBundle::GetReadyFuture()` on deleted or donated bundles instead of returning a cached ready future.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Honor xla_cpu_ftz=false in CpuExecutable's legacy execution path

head_commit.message:
Honor xla_cpu_ftz=false in CpuExecutable's legacy execution path

`CpuExecutable::ExecuteAsyncOnStream` enabled FTZ/DAZ unconditionally, and `CpuExecutable::ExecuteThunks` offloaded work to intra-op worker threads that flush denormals for their whole lifetime, so executables compiled with `DebugOptions.xla_cpu_ftz = false` still flushed subnormals to zero when run outside `PjRtCpuClient`. The PjRt path in `xla/pjrt/cpu/cpu_client.cc` already honors the option; this brings the legacy path in `xla/service/cpu/cpu_executable.cc` in line.

When the module sets `xla_cpu_ftz = false`, the caller thread now runs under `ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and the intra-op `Eigen::ThreadPoolDevice` is wrapped so each offloaded task disables FTZ/DAZ and restores the worker's flags afterwards. Executables without an HLO module keep the previous flushing default. The default `xla_cpu_ftz = true` behavior is unchanged.

`DontFlushDenormalThreadPool` duplicates the class of the same name in `xla/pjrt/cpu/cpu_client.cc` to keep this change free of new files and BUILD edits.

Ported from the XLA patch in https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/4018.

Tested: new CPU-only cases in `//xla/tests:local_client_execute_test` cover a small elementwise multiply and a 256x256 dot dispatched to intra-op workers. Both fail without the `cpu_executable.cc` change and pass with it.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029435088

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip token-typed heroes in DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip token-typed heroes in DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2

`HasSupportedShapes` only rejected tuple-shaped operands and nested tuple results, so a hero with a `token[]` operand, a `token[]` result, or a `token[]` tuple result element was still wrapped into a dynamic slice fusion. Only array operands and results can be sliced, and fusion cost analysis cannot count the elements of a token-typed fusion operand. Custom calls that thread tokens to keep side-effecting calls ordered hit this when one of their array operands is a slice.

Require every hero operand, the hero result, and every tuple result element to be an array, and leave any other hero unfused.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029429342

For an AMD kernel it checks that `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` sets `amdgpu-flat-work-group-size` to `N,N`, where `N` is the total number of threads per block (the product of all three thread dimensions, independent of the block counts). No test covers the attributes set for AMD targets: the existing tests cover NVPTX annotation and the cluster-dim checks, and the one test that passes an AMD triple fails before it reaches the AMD branch. The AMDGPU backend uses `amdgpu-flat-work-group-size` to bound the register budget per wave, so a wrong or missing value would silently change codegen.

🧪 Tests

display_title: [ROCm] Integrate hipDNN behind --xla_gpu_enable_hipdnn (phase 1)

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Integrate hipDNN behind --xla_gpu_enable_hipdnn (phase 1)

Adds a hipDNN-backed path for graph convolution, layer norm and forward
scaled-dot-product attention on ROCm, written against the native
hipdnn_frontend API. The whole path is opt-in via --xla_gpu_enable_hipdnn;
with the flag off every op keeps its existing MIOpen lowering.

stream_executor:
- hipdnn_dnn.cc is the only TU that includes hipdnn_frontend.hpp. It
  implements GraphConvolveRunnerFromDesc, NormRunnerFromDesc, a
  HipdnnGraph : se::dnn::DnnGraph and DeserializeGraph. hipDNN plugin
  engines cannot serialize a compiled plan, so DeserializeGraph re-plans
  with heuristic mode A, which is deterministic and reselects the engine
  the compiler picked.
- miopen_plugin links with -Wl,--exclude-libs,libstdc++fs.a. The sysroot
  ships GCC 8, whose std::filesystem lives in a separate archive and has a
  different path layout than the modern libstdc++. Re-exporting those
  definitions made hipblaslt and librocblas bind to them and segfault in
  std::filesystem::path::_M_split_cmpts().

Compiler:
- hipdnn_conv_rewriter promotes plain forward convolutions to
  __cudnn$convForwardGraph. Reversed windows are left alone: hipDNN ships
  no engine for true convolution, and MIOpen does not serve the graph
  target, so promoting one would strand it with no fallback.
- hipdnn_custom_call_compiler builds and serializes attention graphs for
  __cudnn$fmha*, mirroring CuDnnCustomCallCompiler. When hipDNN is off,
  AMDGPUCompiler::RunCudnnCompilerPasses reports Unimplemented at compile
  time instead of letting the thunk fail with a missing-graph error.
- CudnnNormRewriter is generalized from CudaComputeCapability to
  GpuComputeCapability and runs for ROCm in a pre-pipeline, matching where
  NVPTX runs it relative to GemmRewriter.

Autotuner:
- New HIPDNN backend, registered in factory_rocm.cc. MIOpenBackend no
  longer claims the graph convolution target.

Tests:
- cudnn_norm_rewriter_test was tagged cuda-only, leaving the generalized
  pass with no ROCm coverage. Its cases are device-agnostic, so only SetUp
  needed generalizing; all 19 pass on gfx950.
- factory_test's ROCm backend count goes 6 -> 7, plus an explicit HIPDNN
  case.

Verified on MI355X (gfx950): 23 ROCm test targets pass, and conv, layer
norm and attention each match a CPU reference with the flag on and off.
hipDNN 0.4 has no backward attention engine, so SDPA is inference-only.

head_commit.message:
PR #52912: Gate frontend annotation to call during XLA building

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52912

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR ensure that the frontend-attribute assignment scope only influences the appropriate function call and not other instructions that are created when lowering the function call (e.g. get-tuple-elements/GTE).

🎯 Justification
This change is important because it impacts the scheduling behavior of operations. If somebody had an async collective followed by an async GTE (which is the bug which lead to this problem), the XLA scheduler could schedule compute during the window of the async GTE when it should have been scheduled during the async collective. As a result, this PR prevents that issue from happening via a formal fix (the lowering change).

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No speedup benchmarks as not a performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
This PR validates that GTE/Tuple instructions aren't generated with these async annotations when they are lowered from MLIR HLO to HLO via additions of tests.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests as no new optimizations were added.

display_title: [XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][PJRT][perf] Avoid O(N^2) GetSubSharding traversals in GetShardedShape.

`GetShardedShape` in `xla/pjrt/utils.cc` previously called
`HloSharding::GetSubSharding(shape, index)` for each leaf inside
`ShapeUtil::ForEachMutableSubshape`, re-summing `ShapeUtil::GetLeafCount` across
all preceding tuple siblings on every leaf (`O(N^2)` for an N-element tuple).
Advance a flat leaf index directly across `hlo_sharding.tuple_elements()` in
pre-order DFS (`O(N)`), and handle non-tuple non-tiled shardings (such as
`REPLICATED`) on tuple shapes without crashing in `GetSubSharding`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous collective fusions wrapped in `fusion-start`/`fusion-done` are classified as compute scopes in `ExecutionStreamAssignment` and missed by `GpuAsyncTracker`, spreading peer-communicating fusions across compute streams instead of scheduling them on communication streams.

***Solution:*** Add a single generic `IsCollectiveFusion` predicate in `collective_ops_utils` and use it in `IsExecutionScopeStart`, `IsGpuAsyncStart`/`IsGpuAsyncDone`, `GetResourcesFromInstructionImpl`, and `gpu_hlo_schedule` so async collective fusions are scheduled and assigned as communication ops without leaking codegen details or hero scanning across passes.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

`HloRematerialization` runs `HloCostAnalysis` across every computation in module post order. `HloCostAnalysis::ProcessSubcomputation` previously allocated a nested visitor, rewalked each callee, and copied `hlo_properties_` into the caller on every called computation edge, causing potentially exponential compile time on nested `while` and `conditional` graphs and shared callees.

Cache completed computation totals in `subcomputation_properties_` during `FinishVisit`, evaluate uncached module subcomputations in place while saving traversal state on the stack, invalidate cached totals in `RemoveInstruction` and across module switches, and route `GpuHloCostAnalysis::HandleAsyncStart` through `ProcessSubcomputation`. Generated HLO and compiled executables are unchanged.

Tests:
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:hlo_cost_analysis_test`: pins single visit post order and shared DAG traversal, nested `RevisitInstruction` cache invalidation, partial subgraph visits, single instruction revisit caching, and cross module reuse.
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/backends/gpu/cost_model:gpu_hlo_cost_analysis_test`: pins `async-start` inside `while` across post order and revisit paths.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Add fast branchless FP8 conversions in ExpandFloatOpsPass.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add fast branchless FP8 conversions in ExpandFloatOpsPass.

XLA:CPU previously lowered all 8-bit float conversions through the generic `EmitFloatConversion` fallback. On x86-64 AVX2, that fallback emitted over 100 instructions and 700 bytes of stack spills per vector, making fused FP8 kernels roughly 8x slower than `bf16`.

Add portable, branchless scalar and vector MLIR `arith` lowerings in the CPU `ExpandFloatOpsPass` for all eight 8-bit float formats (`f8E4M3FN`, `f8E5M2`, `f8E4M3`, `f8E3M4`, `f8E4M3FNUZ`, `f8E5M2FNUZ`, `f8E4M3B11FNUZ`, and `f8E8M0FNU`). Conversion from 8-bit float supports `f32`, `f64`, `bf16`, and `f16`, using direct upper-bit truncation for `bf16` and a single shift for `f8E5M2` to `f16`. Conversion to 8-bit float supports `f32`, `bf16`, and `f16` with round-to-nearest-even and no double rounding, clamping the subnormal rounding input for fast-math safety.

On an AMD EPYC 7B13 (67.1M elements, single core), `f32` to `f8E4M3FN` and `f32` to `f8E5M2` speed up by 5x, 8-bit float to `f32` speeds up by 1.7x, and fused FP8 elementwise add speeds up by 4x (matching `bf16` memory bandwidth). Verified bit-for-bit across all 2^32 `f32` inputs, all 2^16 `bf16` inputs, and all 2^8 FP8 inputs (including fast-math mode) on x86-64 and ARM64.

Add portable, branchless scalar and vector MLIR `arith` lowerings in the CPU `ExpandFloatOpsPass` for all eight 8-bit float formats (`f8E4M3FN`, `f8E5M2`, `f8E4M3`, `f8E3M4`, `f8E4M3FNUZ`, `f8E5M2FNUZ`, `f8E4M3B11FNUZ`, and `f8E8M0FNU`). Conversion from 8-bit float supports `f32`, `f64`, `bf16`, and `f16`, using direct upper-bit truncation for `bf16` and a single shift for `f8E5M2` to `f16`. Conversion to 8-bit float supports `f32`, `bf16`, and `f16` with round-to-nearest-even and no double rounding, clamping the subnormal rounding input for fast-math safety.

On an AMD EPYC 7B13 (67.1M elements, single core), `f32` to `f8E4M3FN` and `f32` to `f8E5M2` speed up by 5x, 8-bit float to `f32` speeds up by 1.7x, and fused FP8 elementwise add speeds up by 4x (matching `bf16` memory bandwidth). Verified bit-for-bit across all 2^32 `f32` inputs, all 2^16 `bf16` inputs, and all 2^8 FP8 inputs (including fast-math mode) on x86-64 and ARM64.

display_title: [XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

`HloRematerialization` runs `HloCostAnalysis` across every computation in module post order. `HloCostAnalysis::ProcessSubcomputation` previously allocated a nested visitor, rewalked each callee, and copied `hlo_properties_` into the caller on every called computation edge, causing potentially exponential compile time on nested `while` and `conditional` graphs and shared callees.

Cache completed computation totals in `subcomputation_properties_` during `FinishVisit`, evaluate uncached module subcomputations in place while saving traversal state on the stack, invalidate cached totals in `RemoveInstruction` and across module switches, and route `GpuHloCostAnalysis::HandleAsyncStart` through `ProcessSubcomputation`. Generated HLO and compiled executables are unchanged.

Tests:
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:hlo_cost_analysis_test`: pins single visit post order and shared DAG traversal, nested `RevisitInstruction` cache invalidation, partial subgraph visits, single instruction revisit caching, and cross module reuse.
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/backends/gpu/cost_model:gpu_hlo_cost_analysis_test`: pins `async-start` inside `while` across post order and revisit paths.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [PJRT] Support multi-level tiling in TransposePlan.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Support multi-level tiling in TransposePlan.

Hardware layouts for narrow types use nested tiles — for example, `(8, 128)(2, 1)`
for 16-bit elements or `(8, 128)(4, 1)` for 8-bit elements — to pack adjacent
rows into 32-bit words. Previously `TransposePlan` only supported a single
tiling level, so callers had to run a separate repacking pass or emulate inner
tiles with manual dimension splits.

This change generalizes `TransposePlan` to arbitrary tiling depth:
- `Options::input_tiling` and `Options::output_tiling` now accept a list of
  tiling levels (`std::vector<Tiling>`, outermost to innermost, each dividing
  the enclosing level). The deprecated `Options::input_layout` field is removed.
- Loop construction, ordering, parallelization, chunk sizing, and partial-tile
  padding handle any number of tiling levels.
- Size-1 loops are dropped and adjacent contiguous loops are merged before
  picking the inner kernel, so kernel selection sees the real contiguous runs.
- Updates callers and adds unit and randomized tests for 2- and 3-level
  tilings, compact tiles, strided/broadcast inputs, and cache keys.

Performance on existing untiled and single-level tiled benchmarks is neutral
across Arm and x86 (geomean within 0.5% on all five tested CPUs).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1030222240

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [xla:cpu] mark kernel and comparator return values noundef

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] mark kernel and comparator return values noundef

Clang marks scalar and pointer return values of C++ functions noundef,
including at the host's calls to XLA:CPU kernels and sort comparators.
Mark them noundef on the callee side too.

This is needed for msan: with eager checks, which Clang enables by
default (-fsanitize-memory-param-retval), the caller ignores the shadow
of noundef return values. Without noundef on the callee side,
msan-instrumented XLA:CPU code would pass that shadow anyway, and
uninitialized comparator results would go unreported. With noundef, the
callee checks its return value instead.

display_title: [XLA] Order custom interference buffers by size in topological and merge passes

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Order custom interference buffers by size in topological and merge passes

## Problem

Under `BufferOrder::kTopological` and `FAST_MERGE` (`BufferOrder::kLiveRangeStart`), custom interference buffers are assigned in topological or start time order rather than descending size order. When a later buffer is larger than an earlier compatible buffer, the existing allocation is too small and a new allocation is created.

## Change

When `buffer_order` is not `BufferOrder::kBiggestFirst` and a non fixed offset buffer has custom interference, `AssignBuffersForGlobalComputations` adds a tier comparator. Entry computation parameters run first, custom interference buffers run second in descending size order, and remaining buffers run third.

`FastMergeBufferAllocationsManagerForComputationsWithoutOrdering` assigns custom interference buffers ahead of `UpdateLiveness` using color indexed sorted sets, skipping aliased entry parameters when `must_not_live_out` holds. Occupied custom interference intervals are queued in `pending_reservations_` so regular buffers can reuse dead gaps. `RecordAllocationUse` checks sweep line membership so aliased entry parameters stay out of `active_allocations_`. When no `FAST_MERGE` color buffer has custom interference, `fast_manager` disables this path. `CompareSize` now takes `BufferAssignment*` directly. Existing programs without custom interference buffers do not change behavior.

## Tests

- `//xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`: covers ascending size consolidation (`kTopological`/`SPATIAL`, `kLiveRangeStart`/`FAST_MERGE`, `kBiggestFirst`/`SPATIAL`) and aliased entry parameter reuse (`FAST_MERGE`, `SPATIAL`).
- `//xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`: covers `FAST_MERGE` dead gap reuse, two way best fit with `must_not_live_out`, reservation eviction, non entry `kWhile` parameters, `kBiggestFirst` preservation, fixed offset exclusion, and no op behavior.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous collective fusions wrapped in `fusion-start`/`fusion-done` are classified as compute scopes in `ExecutionStreamAssignment` and missed by `GpuAsyncTracker`, spreading peer-communicating fusions across compute streams instead of scheduling them on communication streams.

***Solution:*** Add a single generic `IsCollectiveFusion` predicate in `collective_ops_utils` and use it in `IsExecutionScopeStart`, `IsGpuAsyncStart`/`IsGpuAsyncDone`, `GetResourcesFromInstructionImpl`, and `gpu_hlo_schedule` so async collective fusions are scheduled and assigned as communication ops without leaking codegen details or hero scanning across passes.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [PJRT] Fuse output tile padding into BuildTransfer at the tile boundary.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Fuse output tile padding into BuildTransfer at the tile boundary.

Previously, `Planner::BuildChunkPlan` emitted output `tile_padding` fills as a
separate second pass (`BuildPadding`) over the entire chunk after
`BuildTransfer` finished. On arrays larger than L2/L3, this revisited cold
partial edge tiles after the transfer had already evicted them.

This change computes `pad_idx` in `ChunkPlanBuilder` as the first loop writing
inside a single output tile (`0 < ldb < tile_bytes`, or a 2D-kernel inner axis
stepped by `inc > 1`), and emits `BuildPadding(idx, partial)` immediately after
the transfer of `chunk_loops[idx..]` inside `BuildTransfer`:
- Outer batch and tile-exterior loops remain outside `pad_idx`, so each partial
  tile is padded while still hot in cache and full tiles run zero padding ops.
- All inner loops of the tile stay inside `BuildPadding`, preserving full
  `Fill1D` coalescing.
- Simplifies `Planner::BuildChunkPlan` to a single `builder.BuildTransfer(...)`
  call.
- Adds batched, transposed, and non-power-of-two output tile-padding unit tests
  and adds output tile-padded cases to `BenchmarkCases()` in `transpose_test.cc`.

display_title: [XLA] Use i64 offsets for large ShardedToUnreducedOp exports.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use i64 offsets for large ShardedToUnreducedOp exports.

Exporting `sdy.sharded_to_unreduced` previously hardcoded `i32` for the `stablehlo.dynamic_update_slice` start offsets and truncated each local dimension size via `getI32IntegerAttr`. When a padded output dimension exceeds `INT32_MAX`, the local dimension constant or `offset * localDimSize` product overflows `i32` and wraps negative, clobbering shard 0's slice.

We now select `i64` for the slice offsets, convert each sharded dimension's coordinate to `i64`, and materialize the zero and local-dimension constants via `createScalarIntConstant` whenever the local output shape requires 64-bit indices, keeping `i32` for smaller shapes.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Move BF16 dot demotion to a dataflow-based post-CSE pass.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Move BF16 dot demotion to a dataflow-based post-CSE pass.

***Problem:*** Demoting BF16-exact F32 dots locally in DotOperandConverter before HloCSE duplicates shared materialized F32 operands in HBM when another consumer keeps the F32 value alive and misses BF16-exact values flowing through control flow.

***Solution:*** Extract lossless BF16 dot demotion into a post-simplification, pre-DotMerger HloDataflowAnalysis pass (DotBf16Demotion) that propagates BF16-exactness forward across data movement and control flow and enforces via a single-BFS F32 constraint graph that materialized F32 buffers are either narrowed in-place or kept F32 everywhere, bypassing only already-materialized BF16 converts and scalar constants.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Disable kCFI checks on client-side PJRT C API and plugin profiler calls.

head_commit.message:
Disable kCFI checks on client-side PJRT C API and plugin profiler calls.

When a client built with Universal CFI (-fsanitize=kcfi) invokes function
pointers provided by a separately built or prebuilt PJRT/profiler plugin
without kCFI type hashes (such as prebuilt libtpu.so), indirect calls across
the C ABI boundary trap with SIGILL.

Wrap the raw C function-pointer invocations in a file-local
ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI `NoCfiCall` helper so CFI checks are skipped
only for the cross-plugin indirect calls while preserving CFI checks on all
surrounding C++ calls. Covers the five files exercised by failing tests:
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_helpers.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_status_utils.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_abi_version_helpers.cc
- xla/backends/profiler/plugin/plugin_tracer.cc
- jaxlib/xla.cc

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Compare number of HIP GPU compute units correctly.

head_commit.message:
Check if either WGP or CU mode's CU count is right.

On newer GPUs, we have 2 operating modes: CU mode and Workgroup mode.
Workgroup mode is the default one for Radeon GPUs, starting with RDNA 2
architecture. However, this mode makes HIP CPP API report number of
available CUs as only half of those really existing on the machine.
There is no runtime HIP API to determine whether the report made for WGP
mode or for CU mode. Therefore, for newer GPUs we expect that at least
one of two possible options in the check is valid.

[XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Dot rewriters that replace a dot with new instructions now derive the new dots
and the replacement via SetupDerivedInstruction, so they inherit the original
dot's metadata and frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This
covers DotAlgorithmRewriter (including the FP8xN decomposition in
hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc), ScaledDotRewriter, SplitkRewriter,
and GemmFusionSwapOperands. When ScaledDotRewriter computes the dot in a wider
type, the convert back to the scaled dot's type, which replaces it, is derived
from it too.

`ConvertToHloModule::LowerFunctionCall` and `LookUpSymbol` in

`module_.lookupSymbol<mlir::func::FuncOp>(...)` on every call and region-callee

`PrepareForExport` without mutating top-level module symbols, cache an

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

Currently XLA executes CUDA CUB sorts via FFI custom calls to `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, which ties the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and prevents embedding sort kernels in AOT artifacts.

So this change adds the sharded `embeddable_cuda_library(..., register_with_cudart = False)` kernel infrastructure under `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/` together with the unified single-tile radix sort kernels (covering both unbatched and batched segments that fit in a single thread block) across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Each device `XlaChainedPolicy` is built from `cub_sort_policy.h` and checked with `static_assert`s so host planning and compiled single-architecture CUBINs stay in lockstep across CCCL versions.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

head_commit.message:
Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

Updates `.github/workflows/bazel_dependency_violations.yml` to run 3 parallel
jobs—one per build configuration:
- `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: consolidates the 3 CPU checks (`gpu`,
  `cuda-only`, `rocm-only`) into separate steps sharing one warm Bazel server,
  saving ~2 cold runner invocations per PR while preserving per-tag step
  reporting and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` output.
- `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build` (`--config=cuda_clang`)
- `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build` (`--config=rocm_clang_hermetic`)

Extracts the per-tag `bazel cquery` check into
`build_tools/dependencies/check_dependency_violations.sh`, triggers `cquery`
when the workflow or dependency-check scripts themselves change, and bumps the
job timeout from 10 to 15 minutes to accommodate the hermetic ROCm download.

Observed GitHub Actions durations (when build/config files change):
- Before (3 separate CPU jobs): ~3m 20s – 5m 30s each (~11m 50s – 12m 30s total
  runner time; ~5m wall-clock).
- After (3 parallel jobs across CPU, CUDA, and ROCm):
  - `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: ~3m 30s – 3m 45s (the 2nd and 3rd `cquery`
    steps take only ~1–4s on the warm Bazel server, saving ~8.5 runner-min).
  - `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build`: ~4m 10s – 6m 05s.
  - `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build`: ~6m 40s – 7m 10s (~8m headroom under
    the 15-minute timeout).
  - Total: ~14m 30s – 16m 45s runner time (~7m wall-clock) for all 3 configs.

Temporarily keeps lightweight pass-through stub jobs (~5s each on
`ubuntu-latest`) for the legacy `no-cuda-only-targets-in-cpu-build` and
`no-rocm-only-targets-in-cpu-build` check names during the transition; a
follow-up change removes them once CI configs stop waiting on those names.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Schedule async collective fusions on communication streams.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous collective fusions wrapped in `fusion-start`/`fusion-done` are classified as compute scopes in `ExecutionStreamAssignment` and missed by `GpuAsyncTracker`, spreading peer-communicating fusions across compute streams instead of scheduling them on communication streams.

***Solution:*** Add a single generic `IsCollectiveFusion` predicate in `collective_ops_utils` and use it in `IsExecutionScopeStart`, `IsGpuAsyncStart`/`IsGpuAsyncDone`, `GetResourcesFromInstructionImpl`, and `gpu_hlo_schedule` so async collective fusions are scheduled and assigned as communication ops without leaking codegen details or hero scanning across passes.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_types.{h,cc}` (shared key/value type support checks used by both `SortRewriter` and `cub_sort_planner`, replacing the duplicated predicate in `sort_rewriter.cc`).
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

display_title: [XLA:Python] Add backend_config dedup to as_serialized_hlo_module_proto

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Python] Add backend_config dedup to as_serialized_hlo_module_proto

Problem: `HloModule.as_serialized_hlo_module_proto()` always calls
`HloModule::ToProto()` with default `HloProtoOptions`, inlining every
instruction's `backend_config`. On large unrolled modules with repeated custom
calls, the serialized `HloModuleProto` can exceed the 2 GiB protobuf limit and
fail serialization.

Solution: Expose optional `deduplicate_backend_config` (default `False`) and
`min_backend_config_size` (default `0`) arguments on
`HloModule.as_serialized_hlo_module_proto()` in `xla/python/hlo.cc` and
`xla/python/_hlo.pyi`, rejecting negative `min_backend_config_size` with
`InvalidArgument`. Default behavior is unchanged.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029918971

display_title: Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

head_commit.message:
Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

Updates `.github/workflows/bazel_dependency_violations.yml` to run 3 parallel
jobs—one per build configuration:
- `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: consolidates the 3 CPU checks (`gpu`,
  `cuda-only`, `rocm-only`) into separate steps sharing one warm Bazel server,
  saving ~2 cold runner invocations per PR while preserving per-tag step
  reporting and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` output.
- `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build` (`--config=cuda_clang`)
- `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build` (`--config=rocm_clang_hermetic`)

Extracts the per-tag `bazel cquery` check into
`build_tools/dependencies/check_dependency_violations.sh`, triggers `cquery`
when the workflow or dependency-check scripts themselves change, and bumps the
job timeout to 15 minutes to accommodate the hermetic ROCm download.

Temporarily keeps lightweight pass-through stub jobs for the legacy
`no-cuda-only-targets-in-cpu-build` and `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cpu-build`
check names during the transition; a follow-up change removes them once CI
configs stop waiting on those names.

display_title: [PJRT] Make Plan leaves self-describing in transpose_plan.cc.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Make Plan leaves self-describing in transpose_plan.cc.

NFC.

- Adds `Plan::Interleave` and `Plan::Deinterleave` leaf nodes and stores
  `elem_size` and `inner_block_elems` directly on `Plan::Transpose2D`.
- Moves splitting of non-block-aligned 2D tiles (into a SIMD-aligned main block
  plus remainder strips) from `ChunkPlanBuilder` into `Plan::MakeTranspose2D`.
- Replaces `FormatPlan` with `Plan::Format`, removes the plan-level kernel and
  element-size parameters from `FlattenPlan` and `PlanFlattener`, and simplifies
  `SelectTranspose2DOp` to a direct lookup using each leaf's resolved block size.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ParseFatbinPtxArchs helper to cuda_elf_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ParseFatbinPtxArchs helper to cuda_elf_utils

Adds `ParseFatbinPtxArchs` to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_elf_utils.{h,cc}` (with unit tests in `cuda_elf_utils_test.cc`) to extract the unique compute capabilities (including accelerated and family-compatible feature extensions from `FatEntryHeader::flags`, using new `kFatbinFlagAccelerated` and `kFatbinFlagFamilyCompatible` constants in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_fatbin.h`) of embedded PTX entries from a CUDA fatbinary container, reusing shared fatbinary entry iteration and compute-capability decoding helpers. This lets callers validate embedded PTX fallback architectures without duplicating fatbinary container parsing logic.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

Currently XLA executes CUDA CUB sorts via FFI custom calls to `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, which ties the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and prevents embedding sort kernels in AOT artifacts.

So this change adds the sharded `embeddable_cuda_library(..., register_with_cudart = False)` kernel infrastructure under `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/` together with the unified single-tile radix sort kernels (covering both unbatched and batched segments that fit in a single thread block) across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Each device `XlaChainedPolicy` is built from `cub_sort_policy.h` and checked with `static_assert`s so host planning and compiled single-architecture CUBINs stay in lockstep across CCCL versions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028243212

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add pure-C++ CUB sort policy and planner

Currently XLA queries CUB host dispatch APIs at compile time to determine radix sort scratch sizes, and falls back to precomputed per-device lookup tables during deviceless compilation. That ties compilation to a live GPU or checked-in tables and prevents emitting self-contained AOT sort thunks.

So this change adds:
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_types.{h,cc}` (shared key/value type support checks used by both `SortRewriter` and `cub_sort_planner`, replacing the duplicated predicate in `sort_rewriter.cc`).
- `ScratchBumpAllocator` in `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/scratch_bump_allocator.{h,cc}` with unit tests for aligned scratch sub-buffer layout and overflow checking.
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_policy.h` (pinned tuning policies across SM50 to SM100 matching CUB `RegBoundScaling` and Hopper/Blackwell small-key tables).
- `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/cub_sort_planner.{h,cc}` (a pure-C++ planner that selects the sort mode, allocates 256B-aligned scratch sub-ranges, partitions large 1D sorts into Onesweep portions, and schedules non-destructive ping-pong passes without requiring a GPU or CUDA headers).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028918425

display_title: Move LowerPdlWaitPass to GPU emitters transforms

head_commit.message:
Move LowerPdlWaitPass to GPU emitters transforms

LowerPdlWaitPass only operates on xla_gpu PDL ops and lowers them to NVVM
griddepcontrol ops. Moving it alongside InsertPDLPass in
xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms removes the
@llvm-project//mlir:NVVMDialect dependency from the shared
//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes library.

Changes:
- Move lower_pdl_ops.cc and tests/pdl.mlir to
  xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/.
- Move LowerPdlWaitPass into namespace xla::gpu and rename its pass flag from
  -xla-lower-pdl-wait to -xla-gpu-lower-pdl-wait.
- Update callers in mlir_kernel_emitter.cc and compilation_pipeline.cc, and
  update the PDL lit tests.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029946086
